newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Feralloys to begin work on new plant.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Feralloys to begin work on new plant.

text.p: South African ferroalloy producer Feralloys says it will start building a new refining plant in March after entering into a joint venture with Japan's Sumitomo Corp and Mizushima Ferroalloy Company to refine 30,000 tonnes of ferro-manganese annually for export.

"We expect building on the refining plant to begin at the end of March and for the first three years it will produce about 30,000 tonnes of refined ferro-manganese per annum," Feralloys general manager Bryan Broekman told Reuters.

The deal reached in September gives Sumitomo 10 percent and Mizushima -- a unit of Kwasaki Steel Corp -- a 40 percent share in the new plant which is expected to be commissioned by the end of this year.
Broekman said Feralloys -- a subsidiary of Associated Manganese Mines of South Africa Ltd would hold 50 percent.
The venture would see capital expenditure of $12.8 million which excluded a working capital of up to $8 million, he said.

Feralloys produces high carbon ferro-manganese at its Cato Ridge plant near Pietermaritzburg. It is spending a further 90 million rand ($20 million) on building two additional furnaces to complement the four existing ones, he said.
"With all six furnaces operational we should be producing about 250,000 tonnes of high carbon ferro-manganese a year. About 37,000 tonnes of this will go to the refining plant," Broekman said.
The new furnaces are expected to be commissioned by July.
The technology for the refining process by which oxygen is blown through molten high carbon ferro-manganese to burn off carbon has come from Mizushima.
"We hope to build up tonnage as we penetrate more markets," said Broekman, adding Sumitomo had an extensive sales network to market the product.
"Most if not all of the refined product will be exported to the Far East, Europe and the United States," he said.
Refined ferro-manganese is used in the stainless steel industry.
